newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing
prices and are annual percentage rates.
Volume fell to 2.5 billion yuan from 3.7 billion yuan last
Friday, with the seven-day contract the most active.
Traders said many rates moved down today mainly due to ample short-term money supply nationwide, which had prompted most financial institutions to be net lenders on the market.
Beijing's clampdown on the stock markets today also had some impact on the interbank market with some securities houses and brokerages ceasing to borrow money, traders said.
But the impact was limited because the major funds flowing into the stock markets had come from the treasury bill repurchase market rather than the interbank market, they said.
"Most financial institutions have enough money with individual bank deposits continuing to surge in recent months," said one trader.
"Non-bank financial institutions which used to be borrowers turned into net lenders today, depressing the rates," said a second trader. "But trading was not active, and demand was limited."
Traders expect the rates to go slowly down in the short term.
